concepts.title: When a neural network is a poor choice
concepts.outcome: Judge when a tree ensemble or a simpler model is the better choice than a neural network, especially on small tabular data.

keyPoints.text: Unlike neural networks, decision forests consume tabular data natively, with no need for preprocessing such as feature normalisation or one-hot encoding, or for imputing missing values.

keyPoints.text: Decision forests are not well suited to consuming unstructured data such as images or text directly; workarounds exist, but neural networks generally handle such data better.

keyPoints.text: Decision forests are sample efficient, suiting small datasets and those with a high ratio of features to examples, and they typically make predictions faster than comparable neural networks.

A network's layers each apply an activation function.

Gradient descent minimises the loss.
Local minima are a property of the surface gradient descent searches.
